subject: [PATCH v3] mm: remove min_free_kbytes adjustment for THP

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary: Reviewer confirmed that they had issues with 512M pageblocks on ARM 64K base page size, leading them to switch to 2M pageblock size in Meta production.
reviews.raw_body:
Yes, just to confirm above, unfortunately, there were too many problems
we were seeing in Meta production with 512M pageblock size for arm 64K
base page size and just had to switch to 2M.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Yan asked for elaboration on the problems described by Johannes Weiner, indicating a desire to understand the technical issues in more detail.
reviews.raw_body:
Do you mind elaborating on the problems? Johannes has given good arguments.
I would like to hear more from you, since he said you know more about the
issues.

Thanks.


Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
Lorenzo questioned the magnitude of min_free_kbytes adjustment, stating that it's unclear how much to retain, and that retaining current values isn't an argument in itself.

Reviewer Lorenzo questioned the timing of removing min_free_kbytes adjustment for THP, suggesting that compaction may need improvement first.

Reviewer Lorenzo raised concerns that removing min_free_kbytes adjustment for THP may not be sufficient to address the ARM 64k page problem, suggesting a more comprehensive rethinking of the mechanism is needed before making such changes.

Lorenzo expressed skepticism about the patch's chances of being accepted, referencing previous rejections and suggesting an alternative proposal to cap huge page size reserves at a certain threshold.

Reviewer Lorenzo expressed concern that the patch may be perpetuating outdated practices and suggested re-examining the reasoning behind set_recommended_min_free_kbytes()

The reviewer notes that removing min_free_kbytes adjustment for THP redefines the size of page blocks while the rest of the THP code still treats PMDs as first-class citizens, and wonders if Kiryl's work to make PMDs not first-class citizens would make this change more reasonable.
sentiment_signals: concerns about persistence of outdated practices
reviews.raw_body:
I mean in general, yes, but the question is how much. This isn't really an
argument for retaining what we have, and as you say below, it's not really
clear what how much is.

---

I wonder whether compaction needs to be improved before we can do that
sanely?

---

I agree having 512 MiB page blocks on 64-KiB arm64 is a bad idea, but I
feel like the entire mechanism needs some degree of rethinking before that
kind of change is done.

Like I said in my other reply, I see this problem as consisting of the
short term (resolving real world pain people experience now) vs. the long
term (reworking compaction, reclaim, and how page blocks function).

---

I mean you're not alone :) we've had a whole host of proposals all of which
were rejected, and you just rejected another...

This is why I suggested the 'if you are concerned about reserves being >X
then cap them at X' proposal.

(v2 of this patch)

https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20260831075635.2244437-1-noren@nvidia.com/

That way nobody is changed, and only really huge page size gets capped.

I mean that's still a possible short-term way forward given this approach
was rejected?

---

See other mail for thoughts on this :) I mean I share your concerns, but I
worry that we continue to persist in doing things because 'that's how they
were always done'.

---

Well it doesn't make it a non-issue, it redefines the size of page blocks
while the rest of the THP code continues to treat PMDs as first class
citizens.

I wonder if Kiryl's work to make PMD _not_ be the 1st class citizen of THP
will make such a change more reasonable.

Perhaps he has thoughts?

--
Cheers, Lorenzo

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary: Reviewer Usama Arif reported that on GPU hosts during AI-training checkpointing, they experienced significant latency spikes and workload timeouts due to unmovable memory and order-0 allocations falling back to MIGRATE_MOVABLE free lists, leading to contaminated movable pageblocks with unmovable pages that caused sustained compaction activity.
reviews.raw_body:
The issue that finally pushed us toward 2 MiB pageblocks occurred on
GPU hosts during AI-training checkpointing. We observed significant
latency spikes and workload timeouts.

These hosts had substantial unmovable memory, and order-0 allocations
from TCP paths repeatedly fell back to MIGRATE_MOVABLE free lists.
With 512 MiB pageblocks, try_to_claim_block() often could not meet
the half-pageblock threshold, so allocation fell through to stealing
individual pages.

This contaminated very large movable pageblocks with unmovable pages.
Compaction then repeatedly scanned those pageblocks but could not
evacuate the unmovable allocations. We observed sustained compaction
activity during the latency spikes.

2026-09-02.patch_summary: This patch removes the adjustment of min_free_kbytes for Transparent Huge Pages (THP) in Linux, as it is deemed unnecessary and potentially problematic on certain ARM configurations.
